landmarks.name: Killam Memorial Library
facts: It claims to be the largest academic library in Atlantic Canada.
Construction began in 1966 and finished in 1971, funded by a $30 million gift in memory of a financier.

landmarks.name: Dalhousie Arts Centre
facts: Its lowest level has housed the university's public art gallery since 1971.

landmarks.name: Shirreff Hall
facts: It is a historic women's residence on the Studley campus.

landmarks.name: DalPlex
facts: It is the main fitness and recreation complex, with a pool and an indoor track.

landmarks.name: Marion McCain Arts and Social Sciences Building
Weldon Law Building and Law Library
Collaborative Health Education Building
facts: It was completed in 2015, one of the newest buildings on campus.

landmarks.name: Risley Hall
facts: Its floors compete every year in a week-long contest called the Prez Cup.

landmarks.name: Student Union Building
facts: Students know it as the SUB; it is the centre of student government and clubs.
It opened on November 8, 1968, after a 1960 referendum in which 90% of voters backed it.

landmarks.name: Goldberg Computer Science Building
facts: It houses the faculty that teaches programming and software.
It took its current name in June 2008 in recognition of a donation.

landmarks.name: Forrest Building
facts: The university moved into it in 1887; it took its current name in 1919.

landmarks.name: Alexandra Hall
facts: It is the traditional women's residence of the University of King's College.
It became co-ed for the first time in 2006.

landmarks.name: Chase Building of Math and Statistics
King's Library
facts: It holds rare Anglican church documents, original artwork and Renaissance and medieval books.

landmarks.name: Arts & Administration Building
facts: Its famous cupola was restored using the original blueprints.
